entities.summary: Antanas Purėnas was a prominent Lithuanian organic chemist and politician born in Rokiškis, Lithuania on February 16, 1881, and died in Vilnius, Lithuania on November 5, 1962. He was a leading figure in the Lithuanian independence movement and served as the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Lithuanian government-in-exile. Purėnas was also a key researcher in the field of organic chemistry, making significant contributions to the development of the Lithuanian chemical industry. His work had a lasting impact on the country's chemical sector, paving the way for Lithuanian scientists to make groundbreaking discoveries. Purėnas's legacy extends beyond his scientific achievements, as he played a crucial role in promoting Lithuanian culture and language abroad, helping to preserve the country's heritage for future generations. His commitment to the Lithuanian people and his contributions to the country's development have cemented his place in Lithuanian history.
